sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Akhtar Uddin died in HMP Wandsworth on Christmas Day 2021 whilst serving a sentence for breaching a Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measure (TPIM). An inquest jury at Inner West London Coroner's Court concluded the restrictive order and fears over its reimposition had a substantial impact on his mental state. They also found the prison service failed to provide the support he needed. Jurors noted it was not possible to determine if he intended his death.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This was the first inquest to consider the impact of TPIMs. Evidence revealed prison staff had little awareness of the restrictions, leading to unintentionally cruel treatment. The coroner noted the state assessed the risk Uddin posed to others, but not risks to Uddin himself, highlighting a broader lack of support for subjects.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Coroner Bernard Richmond KC stated he will issue a preventing future deaths report to the government because of concerns about risks to others subjected to terrorism control measures.

sections.text: Researchers re-examined archival data from the Hubble Space Telescope regarding the white dwarf star HS 0209+0832. Representation of south Asian, Middle Eastern, and disabled characters also declined significantly.
Experts warn that children's books lack incidental representation where identity does not drive plots.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A study by Inclusive Books for Children revealed a decline in diverse main characters in UK books for under-10s in 2025. Books with Black main characters fell by 7.8%, while south Asian representation dropped to 1.4%. Books featuring Middle Eastern and North African characters halved to just three, all of which focused on refugee experiences. Disabled main characters in picture books also fell by 60%.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts argue children need stories reflecting their lives to encourage reading. They highlighted a lack of "incidental representation", where diverse characters star in ordinary stories rather than having their identity drive the plot.
